Subject: Pricing follow-up: token volumes & $/1M benchmarking (Redwood vs OpenAI/Anthropic)

Thanks for the demo earlier, Alex + Sara — good conversation. Quick recap and next steps on pricing/volume so we can turn this into a concrete quote and trial plan. I pulled your notes into our template and attached the monthly token report you shared.

Call recap (short):
- Use case: in-product summarization + search enrichment + chatbot support for customers.
- Current pilot: pilot hits ~2-4M tokens/month now (mostly batch summarization).
- Target steady-state (12mo): 20-40M tokens/month; longer-term expansion to 100M+/month if adoption and retention hold.
- Peak latency requirement: P95 < 400ms for short chat flows; some async jobs can be slower.

Specifics we need from you to finalize pricing:
1) Confirm expected steady-state monthly tokens (low/likely/high).
2) Target budget range (monthly): helps us select Hosted vs Dedicated pricing.
3) Which is more important: lowest $/1M tokens (unit cost) or strict latency SLA / private networking?

Preliminary Redwood vs market benchmarking (assumptions: input+output tokens counted, prices indicative on-demand list rates, no enterprise discounts):
- OpenAI (public on-demand, comparable high-cap models): ~ $800-1,200 per 1M tokens for high-cap models (gpt-4 class equivalents).
- Anthropic (on-demand, high-cap): ~ $650-900 per 1M tokens.
- Open-model hosts (self-hosted/hosted open weights): typically $120-350 per 1M tokens depending on infra and batching.

Redwood positioning: for customers with steady 20-40M tokens/month we typically recommend Dedicated reserved capacity or a committed Hosted plan to hit target unit economics in the $150-250 per 1M tokens range (depends on model variant, batching, and KV caching). For short pilots on Hosted (no commit) the on-demand price will be higher.

Attachments: Acme_Monthly_Token_Report.xlsx (your upload) and redwood_pricing_tiers.pdf (high-level).

Next: Can you confirm the "steady-state" and the budget range? If you confirm 30M/mo and budget ~$6-8k/mo we can prepare a 30-day benchmark + draft quote showing Dedicated reserved pricing at the $/1M that moves you below alternative hosts.

Thanks — Neha

Thanks Alex — useful numbers. Based on 30M steady-state and the budget you quoted ($5k-$10k/month), below are a couple concrete scenarios we typically run for customers and the expected $/1M token unit economics. These are illustrative; final pricing depends on model selection, reserved commit length, and exact traffic profile.

Scenario A — Hosted (committed tier, 12-month commit recommended):
- Assumptions: committed 30M tokens/month, Redwood-managed Dedicated capacity in region, model: high-quality open model equivalence.
- Indicative landed price: $180 per 1M tokens (after commit discounts and batching optimizations).
- Monthly cost at 30M: ~$5,400/mo (within your budget band).
- Pros: predictable cost, managed infra, SLA.
- Cons: commit required; slightly higher latency than private on-prem for very tight P95 targets.

Scenario B — On-demand Hosted (no commit):
- Indicative on-demand price: $420-650 per 1M tokens (varies by model variant and region).
- Monthly cost at 30M: $12,600 - $19,500/mo.
- Pros: no commit; fast to start.
- Cons: not cost-effective at scale.

Scenario C — Private / Dedicated (customer-dedicated GPU pool + 12mo commit):
- Indicative landed price for reserved dedicated: $130-160 per 1M tokens depending on model and quantization; assumes some infra contribution from the customer or a larger commit.
- Monthly cost at 30M: ~$4,000 - $4,800/mo.
- Pros: best unit economics, tight latency control, private networking.

Market baseline (for context):
- OpenAI-like on-demand (high-cap models): ~$800-1,200 / 1M tokens (on-demand).
- Anthropic-like on-demand: ~$650-900 / 1M tokens.
- Commodity open-model hosts (heavily optimized): ~$120-350 / 1M tokens depending on batch sizes and caching.

Takeaway and ask: given your budget band ($5k-$10k/mo) the Hosted committed tier at ~$180/1M or a small Dedicated reserved commit (which pushes ~$130-160/1M) are the two paths that align best. If you confirm a target of 30M/month and a preference for Hosted vs Dedicated, I can:
1) Draft a 30-day benchmark plan (we'll run your sample workload, measure P95 latency and per-token cost).
2) Produce a draft quote showing the committed price and break-even vs on-demand.

I attached the redwood_pricing_tiers.pdf (high-level) and included an example cost sheet in the HubSpot link.

Would you prefer we start with a 30-day benchmark (recommended) or should I send a draft committed quote first?

Thanks — Neha
